sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal bribery laws. It asks if a person must hold a formal office to be charged with selling official power for private gain.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the conviction overturned because he lacked a formal government title during the alleged acts.
The government wants the conviction to stand because the side that brought the case exercised official power regardless of his formal title.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that bribery requires a formal agent who exercises authority on behalf of a principal.
The government argues that official power is fluid and can exist without the formal trappings of an office.

paragraphs: This case defines the boundary of federal bribery laws. It determines whether officials can evade prosecution by shedding formal titles while retaining power. The outcome shapes accountability for public servants who trade influence for private gain.
